edges.description: Less WLS means less transport of lipid-modified Wnt proteins to the cell surface.
Less secreted Wnt reduces Wnt signaling in receiving tissues during embryogenesis.
Reduced Wnt signaling in the developing brain limits brain growth.
Limb-bud patterning depends on Wnt signaling.
Kidney development depends on Wnt signaling.
Eye development depends on Wnt signaling.
Hair follicle development depends on Wnt signaling.
Heart development depends on Wnt signaling.
Craniofacial development depends on Wnt signaling.
Tooth development depends on canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling.
Tissue defects follow each tissue's Wnt dependence, and a Wnt agonist partially rescues development.
edges.limitations: Mouse embryology differs from human, and only the abstract of the source is cached, so the specific tissue readouts are not curated.

nodes.description: The chemical chaperone 4-phenylbutyric acid restored the reduced levels of mutant WLS protein in cells. It acts on the unstable protein itself. It has not been tested in animals or patients.

nodes.description: Two damaging WLS alleles are inherited. Most are missense variants in the transmembrane domains or near the C-terminal endoplasmic-reticulum targeting motif. They lower WLS protein stability, and p.Tyr478Cys has recurred in five patients.

nodes.description: Each tissue is affected according to how strongly it depends on Wnt signaling during development, which explains the variable multi-organ pattern. Brain growth, limb patterning, eye, kidney, heart, hair and teeth are all Wnt-dependent.
